title: Avoid loading the author when checking post ownership
bug: Authors get 403 when editing their own posts.

review.why: The PR changes the ownership check from comparing User objects (post.author != current_user) to comparing post.user_id (int) with current_user (User object), which will always evaluate to True and incorrectly deny all edit attempts with 403.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The diff compares post.user_id (int) to token_auth.current_user() (User object), which always fails, causing 403 instead of 200 for the legitimate owner alice_power.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Because c1 blocks the edit with 403, the post text remains the original 'Alice's first post' instead of the edited 'Alice edited her post'.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The feed reflects the unedited post text due to the failed edit from c1.

doppel.summary: The PR introduces a type mismatch (user_id vs User object) that breaks post editing for legitimate owners, causing 403 errors and preventing updates.

suspicions.claim: The ownership check now compares post.user_id (int) to token_auth.current_user() (User object), which will always be False, causing all edit attempts to return 403 Forbidden even for the post author.
suspicions.trigger: 1. POST /api/tokens with HTTP Basic auth (e.g., alice:doppel-pass) to get access_token. 2. Create a post: POST /api/posts with Authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON {"text": "test"}. Note the returned post id. 3. Edit the post: PUT /api/posts/<id> with Authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON {"text": "updated"}. 3. Read response status code and body. Expected before PR: 200 with updated post. Afte
suspicions.evidence: Probe probe_s1_ownership performed the trigger sequence: POST /api/tokens returned 200 in both base and head, POST /api/posts created a post (201) in both, then PUT /api/posts/151 returned 200 in base but 403 in head, confirming the ownership check regression.
